pull_request.title: lib.types: introduce a `fileset` type
pull_request.body:
During [some work on the Fediversity project](https://git.fediversity.eu/Fediversity/Fediversity/pulls/450), I came with the need for a programmatic FileSet type. I used a bit of an ugly workaround, and this PR is here to introduce a clean alternative.

- Update the `_coerce` internal function to expose a pure variant, `_coerceResult`.
- Expose `isFileset` (using the new `_coerceResult`) and `empty`
- Introduce the “FileSet” type.

IMO, what will deserve most attention is:

- My choice for `isFileset`, namely anything that can be passed to `lib.fileset` functions, not just something with `_type == "fileset'`. I could have called it “filesetable” or something, but this is how “FileSet” is used in the documentation.

- My choices for `check` and `merge`, namely `lib.fileset.isFileset` and `lib.fileset.unions`. This is the first time I contribute to `lib.types`, so I am probably not seeing some interactions they might have.

- Whether we even want that change in nixpkgs or whether we feel it belongs downstream where it is actually used.

Closes https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/266366
Related to https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/266356

comment.body:
The pytest-testinfra facilities look interesting and valuable.

However, i suggest to not make `Machine` inherit from it but instead add a testinfra host object as a member to machine by composition. e.g. `machine.testinfra.file("/etc/foo")` (not sure what the best naming is).

The reason why i suggest that is that we get a somewhat messy signature of member methods and objects that mixes `Machine` and `testinfra.host.Host` matters.

In contrast, if the `testinfra.host.Host` capabilities were exposed via a member variable, they would also be nicer to document.

What do you think?

pull_request.title: hydra-check: patch to fix x86_64-darwin, rust 1.88
pull_request.body:
Works around the issue reported in:
- https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/issues/79
	- patched upstream in https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/pull/80)
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/427072 

This is a band-aid that works around the compiler / linker bug that breaks all http requests on x86_64-darwin with rust 1.88. The issue will disappear once rust is bumped to 1.89, so the patch is conditioned on the current rust version (1.88) and should only apply on x86_64-darwin. Expecting no rebuild for other platforms.

Before this patch (in a nixpkgs checkout):
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
Error: error sending request for url (https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals)

Caused by:
    0: client error (SendRequest)
    1: invalid HTTP version parsed
```
After this patch:
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
```

pull_request.title: hydra-check: patch to fix x86_64-darwin, rust 1.88
pull_request.body:
Works around the issue reported in:
- https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/issues/79
	- patched upstream in https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/pull/80)
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/427072 

This is a band-aid that works around the compiler / linker bug that breaks all http requests on x86_64-darwin with rust 1.88. The issue will disappear once rust is bumped to 1.89, so the patch is conditioned on the current rust version (1.88) and should only apply on x86_64-darwin. Expecting no rebuild for other platforms.

Before this patch (in a nixpkgs checkout):
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
Error: error sending request for url (https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals)

Caused by:
    0: client error (SendRequest)
    1: invalid HTTP version parsed
```
After this patch:
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
⧖ nixpkgs → 9b00558  4h ago   ✔ 250415  ✖ 6296  ⧖ 1586  Δ ~     https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817062

✔ nixpkgs → 8aed177  21h ago  ✔ 251662  ✖ 6525  ⧖ 0     Δ +7    https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817046
```

pull_request.title: fetchFromGitHub: add archiveReproducibilityWorkaround option
pull_request.body:
This option fetches tarball from GitHub based on tree hash instead of the tag to get unprocessed data from the repo, and then applies a partial implementation of `export-subst` to replace certain format strings, but unlike Git uses reproducible values for them.
This includes an example of using this in a package affected by this non-reproducibility.

Related issue: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/84312

issue.title: Policy needed for PRs that are seemingly abandoned by their author

labels.name: 6.topic: policy discussion
labels.description: Discuss policies to work in and around Nixpkgs

labels.name: 9.needs: community feedback
labels.description: This needs feedback from more community members.

issue.body:
In https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/426916, it was shown that there are divergent expectations on how to deal with seemingly abandoned PRs; and that there is also no policy for this.

I have no strongly held feelings towards either approach, but lean towards immediately allowing new superseding PRs with the caveat that commits should include the original author as the primary author and the new PR champion as co-author (unless significant changes are made that warrant reversal of primary/co-authorship). This allows for the changes to become unblocked as quickly as possible, while preserving attribution.

CC @eclairevoyant, @ElvishJerricco; thoughts?

issue.body:
Works around the issue reported in:
- https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/issues/79
	- patched upstream in https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/pull/80)
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/427072 

This is a band-aid that works around the compiler / linker bug that breaks all http requests on x86_64-darwin with rust 1.88. The issue will disappear once rust is bumped to 1.89, so the patch is conditioned on the current rust version (1.88) and should only apply on x86_64-darwin. Expecting no rebuild for other platforms.

Before this patch (in a nixpkgs checkout):
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
Error: error sending request for url (https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals)

Caused by:
    0: client error (SendRequest)
    1: invalid HTTP version parsed
```
After this patch:
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
⧖ nixpkgs → 9b00558  4h ago   ✔ 250415  ✖ 6296  ⧖ 1586  Δ ~     https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817062
⧖ nixpkgs → 83e677f  12h ago  ✔ 251672  ✖ 6538  ⧖ 1     Δ +10   https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817056
✔ nixpkgs → 8aed177  21h ago  ✔ 251662  ✖ 6525  ⧖ 0     Δ +7    https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817046
...
```

issue.body:
This option fetches tarball from GitHub based on tree hash instead of the tag to get unprocessed data from the repo, and then applies a partial implementation of `export-subst` to replace certain format strings, but unlike Git uses reproducible values for them.
This includes an example of using this in a package affected by this non-reproducibility.

moveToOutput is non failing if the source file does not exsits. Hence leaving some redundant moveToOutput script in postInstall. We should check outputDev to be more accurate when using moveToOutput.

please also check the outputDev of non-ucx-support openmpi varient by marking x86_64-linux a badPlatform of ucx.

comment.body:
I mean systemd’s `DynamicUser=` feature.
`User=` can remain as-is to specify the name.

With `systemd.services.<NAME>..serviceConfig.dynamicUser = true`, systemd will create an ephemeral user while the service is running and manage file permissions.

According to [RFC 0052] / [this comment], `dyanmicUser` is preferred where it works well.

The primary restriction of dynamicUser is that it can’t share state with other services/users; however, this doesn’t appear (to me) to be an issue for crowdsec.

We’d need to use [systemd’s provided directories][1].

If it’s not viable to use dynamicUser, than the user/group config should stay as-is.

And we wouldn’t create a user/group here
https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/3e9c7e5c0dabf27e365d553630990a64a1f340ab/nixos/modules/services/security/crowdsec.nix#L908-L916

---

I’ll test this out on my system and see if any issues occur if I try to switch it to dynamicUser.

[RFC 0052]: https://github.com/NixOS/rfcs/blob/master/rfcs/0052-dynamic-ids.md
[this comment]: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/0144ce63f81583f02c967f9fecf0b8294cf5a358/nixos/modules/misc/ids.nix#L6-L19
[1]: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.exec.html#RuntimeDirectory=

issue.body:
This PR updates the `sshd` systemd service to use the `notify-reload` service type.
OpenSSH has supported `sd-notify`-based startup and reload since [last year](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/commit/08f579231cd38a1c657aaa6ddeb8ab57a1fd4f5c).
This improves systemd's tracking of service availability, and also enables `systemctl reload sshd`, which is useful for reloading configuration (ex. to reload the host certificate upon renewal).

comment.body:
> > We should probably also add this to `sshd@.service`, otherwise looks good to me :)
> 
> Ubuntu has `sshd.service` as `Type=notify` but `sshd@.service` as `Type=simple`.

Ubuntu is right.
`sshd.service` is a long-running service answering all incoming ssh connections, and the admin might want it to reload its config file from time to time.
In contrast, `sshd@.service` is only started per-connection by systemd, and each instance serves only one session.  I'm not sure if `Type=notify` is even supported for socket-activated units, but it's likely not useful.
So in essence: `sshd@.service` should not be modified in this regard.

issue.title: nixos/buildDotnetGlobalTool: dotnet lambda test tool via buildDotnetGlobalTool doesn't work

labels.name: 0.kind: bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: 6.topic: nixos
labels.description: Issues or PRs affecting NixOS modules, or package usability issues specific to NixOS

issue.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (25.11)

### Describe the bug

dotnet-lambda-test-tool-8.0 built with buildDotnetGlobalTool fails at runtime. One error occurs due to missing Lambda entry assembly, and another due to denied access to /root path, likely due to sandbox or permission issues in a Nix/NixOS context.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use buildDotnetGlobalTool to package Amazon.Lambda.TestTool-8.0.
2. Run dotnet-lambda-test-tool-8.0 --port 5550 in a typical Lambda project directory.
3. Observe runtime crash with different errors in different terminals:
  1. Missing entry assembly.
  2. Denied access to Wine path /root.

### Expected behaviour

The tool should start a local Lambda test server and detect the project’s compiled entry point without crashing or trying to access /root.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
This is from zed terminal

dotnet-lambda-test-tool-8.0 --port 5550
AWS .NET 8.0 Mock Lambda Test Tool (0.16.3) Unknown error occurred causing process exit: Failed to find Lambda project entry assembly in the specified directory (/home/nixhost/millrocious-nixos) at Amazon.Lambda.TestTool.Runtime.LocalLambdaRuntime.Initialize(String directory, IAWSService awsService) in C:\build\Tools\LambdaTestTool\src\Amazon.Lambda.TestTool\Runtime\LocalLambdaRuntime.cs:line 60 at Amazon.Lambda.TestTool.Runtime.LocalLambdaRuntime.Initialize(String directory) in C:\build\Tools\LambdaTestTool\src\Amazon.Lambda.TestTool\Runtime\LocalLambdaRuntime.cs:line 46 at Amazon.Lambda.TestTool.TestToolStartup.Startup(String productName, Action`2 uiStartup, String[] args, RunConfiguration runConfiguration) in C:\build\Tools\LambdaTestTool\src\Amazon.Lambda.TestTool\TestToolStartup.cs:line 74

This is from ghostty terminal

dotnet-lambda-test-tool-8.0 --port 5550
AWS .NET 8.0 Mock Lambda Test Tool (0.16.3)
Unknown error occurred causing process exit: Access to the path '/home/nixhost/.wine/dosdevices/z:/root' is denied.

at System.IO.Enumeration.FileSystemEnumerator`1.CreateDirectoryHandle(String path, Boolean ignoreNotFound)
at System.IO.Enumeration.FileSystemEnumerator`1.DequeueNextDirectory()
at System.IO.Enumeration.FileSystemEnumerator`1.DirectoryFinished()
at System.IO.Enumeration.FileSystemEnumerator`1.FindNextEntry(Byte* entryBufferPtr, Int32 bufferLength)
at System.IO.Enumeration.FileSystemEnumerator`1.MoveNext()
at System.Collections.Generic.List`1..ctor(IEnumerable`1 collection)
at System.IO.DirectoryInfo.GetFiles(String searchPattern, EnumerationOptions enumerationOptions)
at Amazon.Lambda.TestTool.Utils.SearchLatestCompilationDirectory(String debugDirectory) in C:\build\Tools\LambdaTestTool\src\Amazon.Lambda.TestTool\Utils.cs:line 245

at Amazon.Lambda.TestTool.TestToolStartup.Startup(String productName, Action`2 uiStartup, String[] args, RunConfiguration runConfiguration) in C:\build\Tools\LambdaTestTool\src\Amazon.Lambda.TestTool\TestToolStartup.cs:line 72
```

### Additional context

The tool tries to access Windows-like paths via Wine despite being run on native Linux.
This may indicate incorrect runtime targeting or embedded Windows-specific logic.
Tool was built using .NET 8 SDK/runtime via buildDotnetGlobalTool.

### System metadata

- system: "x86_64-linux"
 - host os: Linux 6.12.39, NixOS, 25.11 (Xantusia), 25.11pre832220.c87b95e25065
 - multi-user?: yes
 - sandbox: yes
 - version: nix-env (Nix) 2.28.4
 - channels(root): "nixos"
 - nixpkgs: /nix/store/fdj8dzj61v63p3861kk3gsgcfdsiaghl-nixos/nixos

Closes #346762

We recently began (re-)implementing **graphite-desktop** using the Chromium Embedded Framework.
This PR contains a working **graphite-desktop** package based on that.

The most potentially controversial aspect is the requirement to define a [cef-rs](https://github.com/tauri-apps/cef-rs) compatible `CEF_PATH`. The cef-rs library expects all required libraries, resources, helper binaries, and an `archive.json` describing the downloaded CEF archive to be placed together in a single directory. Closes #346762

We recently began (re-)implementing **graphite-desktop** using the Chromium Embedded Framework.
This PR contains a working **graphite-desktop** package based on that.

The most potentially controversial aspect is the requirement to define a [cef-rs](https://github.com/tauri-apps/cef-rs) compatible `CEF_PATH`. pull_request.title: hydra-check: patch to fix x86_64-darwin, rust 1.88
pull_request.body:
Works around the issue reported in:
- https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/issues/79
	- patched upstream in https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/pull/80)
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/427072 

This is a band-aid that works around the compiler / linker bug that breaks all http requests on x86_64-darwin with rust 1.88. The issue will disappear once rust is bumped to 1.89, so the patch is conditioned on the current rust version (1.88) and should only apply on x86_64-darwin. Expecting no rebuild for other platforms.

Before this patch (in a nixpkgs checkout):
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
Error: error sending request for url (https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals)

Caused by:
    0: client error (SendRequest)
    1: invalid HTTP version parsed
```
After this patch:
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
⧖ nixpkgs → 9b00558  4h ago   ✔ 250415  ✖ 6296  ⧖ 1586  Δ ~     https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817062
⧖ nixpkgs → 83e677f  12h ago  ✔ 251672  ✖ 6538  ⧖ 1     Δ +10   https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817056
✔ nixpkgs → 8aed177  21h ago  ✔ 251662  ✖ 6525  ⧖ 0     Δ +7    https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817046
...
```

comment.body:
> Is it possible in the Rust ecosystem to write in a `Cargo.toml` file that only certain host platforms should compile dependencies differently?

Yeah this is also the first thing I thought about (because there are similar conditional compilation constructs that may be used), but turns out it is not possible (modulo some workarounds[^workaround]); see: https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/4897

[^workaround]: A particular workaround: one can define a [custom compilation profile](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#custom-profiles), but it's impossible to tie the profile to a specific platform, so the profile-switching logic still needs to be implemented in nix.

comment.body:
>  I'll know for sure tomorrow.

The above is indeed the fix.  Now, wait…

As for the other thing, Livebook seems to work fine using only `beamMinimal28Packages`.  I can't find any docs, but as far as I can tell, the only thing different with the `*Minimal*` package set is lack of support for wxWidgets and systemd, neither of which we use for Livebook.  We wouldn't be the first to do this—Akkoma also uses the minimal package set.

Doing this switch reduces Livebook's transitive closure size from 1.2GB to 0.2GB.  This doesn't say anything about the build deps, but I'm hoping for a similarly large reduction.  I'll mint the PR to do this change once master gets back into a good state.

pull_request.title: nixos-install-tools: enable flakes when using nixos-generate-config --flake
pull_request.body:
<!--
^ Please summarise the changes you have done and explain why they are necessary here ^

For package updates please link to a changelog or describe changes, this helps your fellow maintainers discover breaking updates.
For new packages please briefly describe the package or provide a link to its homepage.
-->

Using n-g-c with --flake option will generate a config that is effectively _unbuildable_ with nixos-rebuild (#181471) unless additional options are passed explicitly.
This _will_ cause confusion for new users who aren't aware of what those additional options would be, and in any case, using `--flake` is an explicit statement that the system should support flakes.
Hence, we should enable said features in the config of those who are opting in in this manner.
 
Relevant:

This PR adds a standalone flang package build based on LLVM 19.1.7. It enables building flang out-of-tree by:

pull_request.title: hydra-check: patch to fix x86_64-darwin, rust 1.88
pull_request.body:
Works around the issue reported in:
- https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/issues/79
	- patched upstream in https://github.com/nix-community/hydra-check/pull/80)
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/427072 

This is a band-aid that works around the compiler / linker bug that breaks all http requests on x86_64-darwin with rust 1.88. The issue will disappear once rust is bumped to 1.89, so the patch is conditioned on the current rust version (1.88) and should only apply on x86_64-darwin. Expecting no rebuild for other platforms.

Before this patch (in a nixpkgs checkout):
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
Error: error sending request for url (https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals)

Caused by:
    0: client error (SendRequest)
    1: invalid HTTP version parsed
```
After this patch:
```console
$ nix run --file . --option system x86_64-darwin hydra-check
Evaluations of jobset nixpkgs/trunk @ https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/trunk/evals
⧖ nixpkgs → 9b00558  4h ago   ✔ 250415  ✖ 6296  ⧖ 1586  Δ ~     https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817062
⧖ nixpkgs → 83e677f  12h ago  ✔ 251672  ✖ 6538  ⧖ 1     Δ +10   https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817056
✔ nixpkgs → 8aed177  21h ago  ✔ 251662  ✖ 6525  ⧖ 0     Δ +7    https://hydra.nixos.org/eval/1817046
...
```

pull_request.title: lib.types: introduce a `fileset` type
pull_request.body:
During [some work on the Fediversity project](https://git.fediversity.eu/Fediversity/Fediversity/pulls/450), I came with the need for a programmatic FileSet type. I used a bit of an ugly workaround, and this PR is here to introduce a clean alternative.

- Update the `_coerce` internal function to expose a pure variant, `_coerceResult`.
- Expose `isFileset` (using the new `_coerceResult`) and `empty`
- Introduce the “FileSet” type.

IMO, what will deserve most attention is:

- My choice for `isFileset`, namely anything that can be passed to `lib.fileset` functions, not just something with `_type == "fileset'`. I could have called it “filesetable” or something, but this is how “FileSet” is used in the documentation.

- My choices for `check` and `merge`, namely `lib.fileset.isFileset` and `lib.fileset.unions`. This is the first time I contribute to `lib.types`, so I am probably not seeing some interactions they might have.

- Whether we even want that change in nixpkgs or whether we feel it belongs downstream where it is actually used.

Closes https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/266366
Related to https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/266356
